label: calorie
request: Track what I eat and how much, with calories, history and trends

runtime.note: development runtime; F22 supplies the signed relocatable bundle

content.text: Track what I eat and how much, with calories, history and trends

content.reply:
I'll build you a food log app: a quick-entry screen, today's running total, day-by-day history, and weekly calorie trends — all kept on your Mac.

Three quick things so it fits how you eat:

1. Should Alpha estimate calories from your description (always marked as an estimate you can correct), or do you prefer typing the numbers yourself?
2. Do you want a daily calorie target to measure against?
3. Calories only, or also protein, carbs and fat?

One limit: I can't send reminders or run anything on a schedule yet, so logging is something you open and do.

interpretation.outcome: A personal food diary on your Mac that records what you ate and how much, with calories, full history and trends over time.
interpretation.main_input: Short entries you type as you eat, e.g. "2 eggs and toast", with calories either estimated for you or typed in.
interpretation.useful_result: A quick-entry screen, today's running calorie total, a browsable history by day, and weekly trends showing whether intake is rising or falling.
important_assumptions: Days run midnight to midnight in your local time
Entries default to the current date and time and can be edited
Everything stays on this Mac until you delete it

questions.question: How should calories get filled in?
options: Alpha estimates from my description (I can correct it)
Both: estimate, but let me overwrite
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the app estimates for you or waits for your numbers.

questions.question: Do you want a daily calorie target, and if so roughly what number?
questions.why_it_matters: A target turns the daily total into 'on track' or 'over', and shapes the trends.

questions.question: Track calories only, or also protein, carbs and fat?
questions.why_it_matters: It changes what you enter each time and what the trends can show.

content.reply: Done — defaults locked in. Alpha will estimate calories from what you type (always labelled as an estimate you can correct), track calories only to keep entry quick, and show plain totals with no daily target for now; you can add one later. You get a quick-entry screen with today's running total, a day-by-day history you can scroll and correct, and trends with daily totals plus a 7-day average. Untracked days show as gaps, not zeros. Everything stays on this Mac. One limit: no reminders or scheduled runs yet, so logging is something you open and do.

interpretation.outcome: A food log app on your Mac: quick entry, today's total, full history and calorie trends.
interpretation.main_input: Short typed descriptions of what you ate and how much, entered as you go.
interpretation.useful_result: Log a meal in seconds, see today's total right away, open any past day, and see whether recent weeks trend up or down.
important_assumptions: Alpha estimates calories from your description and marks them as estimates you can overwrite.
No daily target for now — totals only; a target can be set later.
Calories only, no protein/carbs/fat, so entry stays fast.
A day runs midnight to midnight locally; new entries default to now.
Recent foods are offered for one-tap repeat logging.
Everything stays on this Mac until you delete it.

current_brief.goal: Let the user log what they eat and how much, see calories per entry and per day, browse full history, and see trends over time.
current_brief.success_summary: The user can log a meal in a few seconds, see today's calorie total immediately, scroll back through any past day, and see whether intake is trending up or down over recent weeks.

primary_journey.action: Open the app and type what was eaten and how much, e.g. "2 scrambled eggs, 1 slice toast".
primary_journey.expected_result: Calories are estimated and clearly labelled as an estimate, and the entry is saved with today's date and time.

primary_journey.action: Glance at the top of the screen.
primary_journey.expected_result: Today's running calorie total is shown, with how many entries so far.

primary_journey.action: Correct an entry whose amount or calories looks wrong.
primary_journey.expected_result: The entry updates, today's total recalculates, and the calories are marked as user-confirmed.

primary_journey.action: Open history and pick a past day.
primary_journey.expected_result: All entries for that day are listed with their calories and the day's total.
Daily totals for recent weeks with a 7-day average, average calories per day, and most-logged foods.

data_needs.purpose: The record of everything eaten, when, how much, and its calories.

fields.name: Amount
fields.description: Quantity or portion, e.g. '2 slices', '200 g', '1 bowl'

fields.name: Calories are an estimate
fields.description: True when Alpha estimated the number and the user has not confirmed it

fields.name: Eaten at
fields.description: Date and time of the entry; defaults to now

data_needs.purpose: Holds an optional daily calorie target; left empty by default so the app shows plain totals.

fields.name: Daily calorie target
fields.description: Optional target calories per day; empty means no target

fields.name: Target set on
fields.description: When the target was last changed

data_needs.retention: until the user changes or deletes it

actions.title: Log a food entry
actions.description: Saves what was eaten, the amount, the calories, the meal label and the time. Rejects an entry with no description and asks for an amount when none is given.

actions.title: Estimate calories from the description
actions.description: Reads the description and amount and suggests a calorie number, always labelled as an estimate the user can overwrite. Says it is unsure and asks for a portion when the description is too vague to size.
outputs: Note when the portion is unclear

actions.title: Show a day's entries and total
actions.description: Lists every entry for a chosen day with its calories and adds up the day's total. If a daily target is set later, it also shows over or under that target.
outputs: Over or under target when a target exists

actions.title: Correct or delete an entry
actions.description: Updates the description, amount, calories, meal or time of an existing entry, or removes it, and recalculates the affected day's total. Confirmed calories are no longer marked as an estimate.

actions.title: Show trends over time
actions.description: Charts daily calorie totals across a chosen period with a 7-day rolling average, the average per day, and the most frequently logged foods. Days with no entries are shown as gaps, not zeros.

constraints: Estimated calories are always visibly marked as estimates and are editable.
Calories are the only nutrient tracked; protein, carbs and fat are out of scope for now.
No daily target is set initially; the app works on plain totals until the user sets one.
All data stays on this Mac; nothing is sent anywhere.
Days are bounded midnight to midnight in local time, and days with no entries count as missing, not zero.

acceptance_examples.description: Logging a simple meal fills in estimated calories and updates today's total.

input.What was eaten: 2 scrambled eggs and 1 slice of buttered toast

expected.Saved entry: 2 scrambled eggs and 1 slice of buttered toast, 1 plate, breakfast

acceptance_examples.description: A description with no portion cannot be sized confidently.

expected.Message: Asks how much, offering options like 'small bowl', 'large bowl', '200 g'

acceptance_examples.description: A period containing untracked days shows gaps rather than zeros.

input.Period: last 7 days, with 2 days having no entries

expected.Chart: 5 days plotted, 2 days shown as gaps
expected.Average per day: Calculated from the 5 logged days only, with a note that 2 days were not logged
